lessons.title: Pearson Square Method for Simple Formulations
lessons.body: The Pearson Square is a simple arithmetic method to blend two ingredients to achieve a desired nutrient level, usually protein. It works best when you have two main ingredientsâone high in protein (e.g., fishmeal, soybean meal) and one low (e.g., maize, cassava). For example, you want a 30% protein feed using fishmeal (60% protein) and maize (9% protein). Draw a square, put 30 in the center, 60 top-left, 9 bottom-left. Subtract diagonally: 60-30=30 parts maize, 30-9=21 parts fishmeal. Total parts = 51. So fishmeal is 21/51 â 41.2%, maize is 30/51 â 58.8%. That gives 30% protein. But this is only two ingredientsâreal feeds need vitamins, minerals, oils. Use Pearson Square to fix the protein base, then add 1-2% vitamin premix, 1% mineral premix, and 3-5% vegetable oil for energy. In Africa, common protein sources: fishmeal (55-65% CP), soybean meal (44-48% CP), groundnut cake (40-45% CP), cottonseed cake (32-36% CP). Energy sources: maize (8-9% CP), rice bran (8-12% CP), cassava (2-3% CP). Always test your mix: if you need 35% protein for tilapia fingerlings, use fishmeal (60%) and rice bran (10%): center 35, top 60, bottom 10. Difference: 60-35=25 parts rice bran, 35-10=25 parts fishmeal. So 50:50 mix. That's 35% protein. But rice bran has high fibreâlimit to 30% in tilapia diets. So you might need a third ingredient. Pearson Square is a starting point, not the final answer. For small-scale farmers, itâs cheap and doesnât need software. Write down your calculations, weigh ingredients accurately, and mix thoroughly. A 50 kg batch: 25 kg fishmeal, 25 kg rice bran, plus 0.5 kg vitamin premix, 0.5 kg mineral premix, and 2 kg palm oil. This gives a 35% protein feed suitable for tilapia grow-out. Always keep records of your formulations and the growth results.

lessons.title: Linear Programming for Least-Cost Formulation
lessons.body: Linear programming (LP) is a mathematical method to find the cheapest mix of ingredients that meets all nutrient requirements. Unlike Pearson Square, LP handles many ingredients and multiple constraints (protein, fat, fibre, amino acids, calcium, phosphorus). You set a target for each nutrient (e.g., protein â¥ 30%, fat â¥ 6%, fibre â¤ 8%) and the cost per kg of each ingredient. The LP solver then calculates the least-cost combination. In Africa, you can use free tools like Excel Solver, OpenSolver, or dedicated feed formulation software like WinFeed, FeedSoft, or Bestmix. For example, you have maize (â¦250/kg, 9% CP), soybean meal (â¦600/kg, 44% CP), fishmeal (â¦1200/kg, 60% CP), rice bran (â¦150/kg, 10% CP), and palm oil (â¦800/kg, 0% CP). You want a 30% CP diet for tilapia. Constraints: CP â¥ 30%, fat â¥ 5%, fibre â¤ 8%, lysine â¥ 1.5%, methionine â¥ 0.6%. The LP solver might give: maize 40%, soybean meal 25%, fishmeal 15%, rice bran 15%, palm oil 3%, premixes 2%. Cost per kg = (0.4Ã250)+(0.25Ã600)+(0.15Ã1200)+(0.15Ã150)+(0.03Ã800) = 100+150+180+22.5+24 = â¦476.5/kg. Without LP, a farmer might use 50% fishmeal and 50% maize, costing â¦725/kg. LP saves â¦248.5/kg. For a 1-tonne batch, that's â¦248,500 saved. LP also helps when ingredient prices changeâjust update prices and re-run. In Africa, where fishmeal is expensive and often scarce, LP can substitute with cheaper local proteins like black soldier fly larvae meal (40-45% CP), moringa leaf meal (25-30% CP), or brewersâ spent grain (20-25% CP). But you must set maximum inclusion levels for anti-nutritional factors (e.g., cottonseed max 10% due to gossypol). Start with simple LP in Excel: list ingredients in rows, nutrients in columns, set target values, and use Solver to minimise cost. Always validate the final mix with a lab test if possible.

lessons.title: Software Tools for Feed Formulation
lessons.body: You donât need expensive software to formulate fish feed. Several free or low-cost tools work well in Africa, even offline. For beginners, Microsoft Excel with Solver is powerful. You create a spreadsheet: rows for ingredients (maize, soybean meal, fishmeal, etc.), columns for nutrients (protein, fat, fibre, lysine, methionine, calcium, phosphorus), and a cost column. You set a target row for each nutrient (e.g., protein 30%). Then use Solver to minimise total cost by changing the percentage of each ingredient, subject to constraints (e.g., protein â¥ 30%, fibre â¤ 8%, fishmeal â¤ 20%). Excel Solver comes with most Excel versions; if not, download OpenSolver (free add-in). For more advanced needs, try WinFeed (free trial), FeedSoft (paid but affordable), or Bestmix (widely used in Africa). These have databases of local ingredients and nutrient profiles. If you have no computer, use a smartphone app: âFeed Formulationâ by ILRI (free on Android) or âAquaFeedâ (simple Pearson Square calculator). For farmers with no internet, download the FAOâs âFeed Formulation for Small-Scale Fish Farmersâ PDFâit has tables and step-by-step examples. Another option: use the âTilapia Feed Formulatorâ spreadsheet from WorldFish, which is pre-loaded with African ingredients. Always keep a notebook to record your formulations, ingredient costs, and fish growth. If you use software, save your files and back them up. Many African feed mills use a simple Excel sheet with Solver. For example, a farmer in Ghana uses Excel to formulate a 28% protein diet for Nile tilapia using maize, soybean meal, fishmeal, wheat bran, and palm oil. He updates prices weekly and re-runs Solver. This takes 10 minutes and saves him 20% on feed costs. Start with Excel; itâs free, flexible, and widely available. Watch YouTube tutorials on âExcel Solver feed formulationâ to learn. Once comfortable, you can explore dedicated software.

lessons.title: Setting Nutrient Specifications for Different Species
lessons.body: Different fish species need different nutrient levels. You cannot use the same feed for tilapia, catfish, and carp. Here are practical specifications for common African species. Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus): fingerlings (0.5-10g) need 35-40% protein, 8-10% fat, 5-8% fibre; grow-out (10-200g) need 28-32% protein, 6-8% fat, 8-12% fibre; broodstock need 30-35% protein, 6-8% fat, plus higher vitamin C and E. African catfish (Clarias gariepinus): fingerlings need 45-50% protein, 10-12% fat; grow-out need 35-40% protein, 8-10% fat; broodstock need 40-45% protein. Catfish are carnivorous, so they need more fishmeal or animal protein. Common carp (Cyprinus carpio): fingerlings 35-40% protein, grow-out 25-30% protein. For all species, essential amino acids: lysine and methionine are critical. Tilapia need 1.5-1.8% lysine and 0.6-0.8% methionine in feed. Catfish need 2.0-2.5% lysine and 0.8-1.0% methionine. Minerals: calcium 1.0-1.5%, phosphorus 0.5-0.8% (available phosphorus, not total). Vitamins: add a commercial premix at 0.5-1.0% of diet. In Africa, many farmers use 30% protein for tilapia grow-out, but research shows 28% is enough if amino acids are balanced. Overfeeding protein wastes money and pollutes water. For catfish, donât go below 35% protein. Use local ingredients: fishmeal (60-65% CP), soybean meal (44-48% CP), groundnut cake (40-45% CP), cottonseed cake (32-36% CP), maize (8-9% CP), rice bran (8-12% CP), cassava (2-3% CP). For tilapia, you can replace up to 50% of fishmeal with soybean meal if you add methionine. For catfish, replace no more than 30% of fishmeal. Always test your feed on a small batch of fish before scaling up. Keep records of growth, feed conversion ratio (FCR), and survival. Adjust specifications based on results.

lessons.title: Balancing Amino Acid Profiles
lessons.body: Protein is made of amino acids. Fish donât need protein per seâthey need the right balance of essential amino acids (EAAs). The ten EAAs for fish are: arginine, histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine. If one EAA is deficient, fish cannot use the protein efficiently, and growth slows. The most limiting amino acids in African fish feeds are lysine and methionine, especially when using plant proteins like maize, soybean meal, and groundnut cake. For example, a tilapia diet with 30% protein from maize and soybean meal may be low in methionine. You can add synthetic methionine (DL-methionine) at 0.1-0.3% of diet. Lysine can be added as L-lysine HCl at 0.2-0.5%. To balance amino acids, you need to know the amino acid profile of each ingredient. Tables from FAO or NRC (National Research Council) give these values. For example, fishmeal has 4.5% lysine and 1.8% methionine (per 100g protein). Soybean meal has 2.8% lysine and 0.6% methionine. Maize has 0.3% lysine and 0.2% methionine. So a mix of 50% maize, 40% soybean meal, 10% fishmeal gives: lysine = (0.5Ã0.3)+(0.4Ã2.8)+(0.1Ã4.5) = 0.15+1.12+0.45 = 1.72% of diet? Wait, these are per 100g protein. Better: use actual percentages in feed. If feed has 30% protein, and you want 1.5% lysine in feed, you need 5% lysine in protein. Fishmeal has 7.5% lysine (4.5g/60g protein? Actually fishmeal 60% CP, lysine 4.5% of feed? No, typical fishmeal: 60% CP, lysine 4.5% of feed, methionine 1.8% of feed. Soybean meal: 44% CP, lysine 2.8% of feed, methionine 0.6% of feed. Maize: 9% CP, lysine 0.3% of feed, methionine 0.2% of feed. So for a 30% CP diet, you can calculate. Use software or Excel to check. If deficient, add synthetic amino acids. In Africa, synthetic methionine and lysine are available from feed suppliers. They cost about $3-5 per kg. Adding 0.2% methionine to a 100kg batch costs $0.60-$1.00, but improves growth by 10-20%. Always balance amino acids before increasing protein levelâitâs cheaper to add 0.2% methionine than 5% fishmeal.

lessons.title: Formulating for Different Life Stages
lessons.body: Fish need different feeds at different life stages. You cannot feed the same diet to fry, fingerlings, and broodstock. Hereâs how to formulate for each stage, using Nile tilapia as an example. Fry (0.01-0.5g): need 40-45% protein, 10-12% fat, 3-5% fibre. Feed size: powder or crumble. Use fishmeal (60% CP) as main protein, plus soybean meal, and add 5% cod liver oil or palm oil for essential fatty acids. Include 1% vitamin premix and 1% mineral premix. Fry need high energy and easily digestible protein. In Africa, you can use boiled egg yolk or Artemia for first feeding, but formulated feed is cheaper. Fingerlings (0.5-10g): need 35-40% protein, 8-10% fat, 5-8% fibre. Feed size: 1-2mm pellets. Use 30% fishmeal, 30% soybean meal, 30% maize, 5% rice bran, 3% palm oil, 2% premixes. This gives about 38% protein. Grow-out (10-200g): need 28-32% protein, 6-8% fat, 8-12% fibre. Feed size: 2-4mm pellets. Use 15% fishmeal, 25% soybean meal, 40% maize, 15% rice bran, 3% palm oil, 2% premixes. This gives about 30% protein. Broodstock (adults for breeding): need 30-35% protein, 6-8% fat, plus high vitamin C (500mg/kg) and vitamin E (200mg/kg) for egg quality. Use 20% fishmeal, 25% soybean meal, 35% maize, 15% rice bran, 3% palm oil, 2% premixes, plus extra vitamins. For catfish: fry need 50% protein, fingerlings 45%, grow-out 40%, broodstock 45%. For carp: fry 40%, fingerlings 35%, grow-out 25-30%. Always adjust feed size: fry powder, fingerlings 1-2mm, grow-out 2-4mm, broodstock 4-6mm. In Africa, many farmers use a single 28% protein diet for all stagesâthis wastes money for fry (they grow slower) and overfeeds grow-out (extra protein is excreted). Instead, make two or three formulations: starter (40% CP), grower (30% CP), and finisher (28% CP). Store feeds in cool, dry place. Use within 3 months. Record feed intake and fish growth to adjust formulations.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of the Pearson Square method?
options: A) To calculate the cost of feed ingredients
B) To blend two ingredients to achieve a desired nutrient level
C) To balance amino acids in a diet
D) To determine feed pellet size
quiz.explanation: The Pearson Square is a simple arithmetic method to blend two ingredients to hit a target nutrient level, usually protein.

quiz.q: In Pearson Square, if you want 30% protein using fishmeal (60% CP) and maize (9% CP), what is the ratio of fishmeal to maize?
quiz.explanation: Subtract diagonally: 60-30=30 parts maize, 30-9=21 parts fishmeal, so ratio is 21:30 fishmeal:maize.

quiz.q: Which of these is a limitation of the Pearson Square method?
options: A) It cannot handle more than two ingredients
C) It only works for catfish
D) It cannot calculate protein levels
quiz.explanation: Pearson Square only works with two main ingredients; it cannot handle multiple constraints like fibre, fat, or amino acids.

quiz.q: What does linear programming (LP) do in feed formulation?
options: A) It calculates the cheapest mix that meets nutrient requirements
B) It measures feed pellet size
C) It tests feed for toxins
quiz.explanation: LP finds the least-cost combination of ingredients that satisfies all specified nutrient constraints.

quiz.q: Which tool is free and commonly used for LP feed formulation in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Excel Solver is free (or comes with Excel) and widely used for simple LP formulations.

quiz.q: If a farmer uses LP and saves â¦248.5/kg compared to a manual mix, how much is saved on a 1-tonne batch?
Which of these is a common local protein source in Africa for fish feed?
quiz.explanation: Soybean meal, fishmeal, and corn gluten meal are all used, though availability varies; soybean meal and fishmeal are most common.

quiz.q: What is a key advantage of using software for feed formulation?
options: A) It eliminates the need for ingredients
B) It can handle many ingredients and constraints quickly
C) It guarantees fish will grow faster
D) It replaces the need for vitamins
quiz.explanation: Software like Excel Solver or WinFeed can optimise many ingredients and constraints simultaneously, saving time and money.

quiz.q: Which free smartphone app is mentioned for feed formulation?
quiz.explanation: Both ILRIâs Feed Formulation app and AquaFeed are mentioned as free smartphone tools.

quiz.q: What is a good practice when using feed formulation software?
options: B) Save and back up your files
quiz.explanation: Saving and backing up files ensures you donât lose your formulations and can track changes.

quiz.q: What protein level is recommended for Nile tilapia fingerlings (0.5-10g)?
quiz.explanation: Tilapia fingerlings need 35-40% protein for optimal growth.

quiz.q: What protein level is recommended for African catfish grow-out?
quiz.explanation: Catfish are carnivorous and need 35-40% protein during grow-out.

quiz.q: Which mineral is critical for fish bone development and must be specified in feed?
quiz.explanation: Calcium and phosphorus are critical for bone development; calcium is typically specified at 1.0-1.5%.

quiz.q: For tilapia grow-out, what is the recommended protein range?
quiz.explanation: Tilapia grow-out (10-200g) need 28-32% protein for efficient growth.

quiz.q: Why should you not use the same feed for all life stages?
options: B) Different stages have different nutrient needs
C) It causes fish to change colour
quiz.explanation: Fry, fingerlings, and broodstock have different protein, fat, and vitamin requirements; using one feed wastes money and reduces growth.

quiz.q: Which two amino acids are most limiting in African fish feeds?
quiz.explanation: Lysine and methionine are the most limiting amino acids, especially in plant-based diets.

quiz.q: What is the typical methionine content in fishmeal (per 100g feed)?
quiz.explanation: Fishmeal (60% CP) typically contains about 1.8% methionine in the feed.

quiz.q: If a diet is deficient in methionine, what is a cost-effective solution?
quiz.explanation: Adding 0.1-0.3% synthetic methionine is cheaper than adding fishmeal to correct a deficiency.

quiz.q: What is the recommended inclusion level of synthetic lysine in a deficient diet?
quiz.explanation: L-lysine HCl is typically added at 0.2-0.5% of the diet to correct deficiencies.

quiz.q: Which ingredient has the highest lysine content per 100g feed?
quiz.explanation: Fishmeal has about 4.5% lysine, higher than soybean meal (2.8%) and maize (0.3%).

quiz.q: What is the first step in balancing amino acids?
options: B) Know the amino acid profile of each ingredient
quiz.explanation: You must know the amino acid composition of your ingredients to identify deficiencies.

quiz.q: Why is it cheaper to add synthetic methionine than to increase fishmeal?
options: B) Fishmeal is expensive and adds excess protein
quiz.explanation: Fishmeal is costly and adding it just for methionine also adds excess protein; synthetic methionine is targeted and cheap.

quiz.q: What feed size is recommended for tilapia fry?
quiz.explanation: Fry (0.01-0.5g) need powder or crumble feed because their mouths are very small.

quiz.q: What protein level is recommended for tilapia broodstock?
quiz.explanation: Broodstock need 30-35% protein plus extra vitamins for egg quality.

quiz.q: For African catfish fry, what is the recommended protein level?
quiz.explanation: Catfish fry need 45-50% protein for rapid growth.

quiz.q: What is a practical way to adjust feed for different life stages on a small farm?
options: A) Use one feed for all stages
B) Make two or three formulations (starter, grower, finisher)
quiz.explanation: Making separate starter, grower, and finisher feeds matches nutrient needs and saves money.

quiz.q: How long should formulated feed be stored?
quiz.explanation: Feeds should be used within 3 months and stored in a cool, dry place to prevent spoilage.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a common energy source in African fish feeds?
quiz.explanation: Fishmeal is a protein source, not an energy source; maize, rice bran, and cassava are energy sources.

quiz.q: What is the typical protein content of soybean meal?
quiz.explanation: Soybean meal typically contains 44-48% crude protein.

quiz.q: Why is it important to record feed formulations and fish growth?
options: B) To track what works and adjust for better results
C) It is required by law
quiz.explanation: Records help you identify successful formulations and make data-driven adjustments to improve growth and reduce costs.
